newsitem.title: USA: Simpson defense begins closing arguments.
newsitem.headline: Simpson defense begins closing arguments.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's lead attorney in his civil trial began his closing argument Wednesday, saying the Los Angeles Police Department and the FBI were prejudiced against the former football star.

Attorney Robert Baker said the two law enforcement agencies had spent "thousands and thousands of their dollars...to assist plaintiffs in a civil case," adding, "The FBI and the LAPD don't want a level playing field."

Baker said Simpson's defence team had been unable to get police officers to take the witness stand without first serving them subpoenas, but the plaintiffs' lawyers had received phone calls from officers and FBI agents offering their services. "Is that fair?" he asked the jury.

Simpson was acquitted in 1995 of the June 1994 murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, and is battling a wrongful-death civil lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who seek substantial financial damages.
Baker said police officers called by the plaintiffs to testify in the civil case "contradicted each other and they lied on the witness stand."

Baker's closing argument followed a final summation by the plaintiffs' lead attorney, Daniel Petrocelli, who pleaded with the jury to force Simpson to compensate Goldman's father, Fred Goldman, for the loss of his son. But Baker dismissed Petrocelli's appeal, telling the panel, "You have just been subjected to a ploy for your sympathy."
